title: Background Blur Is About Distance, Not Just Aperture
excerpt: A kit lens at f/3.5 can melt a background just fine. Photographer Jason Vong shows that distance, focal length, and the space behind your subject matter more than owning an f/1.8 prime, and that shooting wide open is often the worse choice anyway.

title: A Sharp 35mm f/1.4 for $829. The Catch Weighs 760 Grams.
excerpt: The new Viltrox 35mm f/1.4 Pro is sharp at f/1.4 right to the corners, PetaPixel's review finds, and it costs $829. The catch is not optical. It is 760 grams hanging off the front of your camera, and whether that trade is worth it depends on which mount you shoot.

title: He Shot a Newsweek Cover and Lost the Copyright
excerpt: Lester LaRue shot a Newsweek cover on the morning of the Oklahoma City bombing, then lost the copyright to his employer. The court ruled the photos were works made for hire, and the lesson for every working photographer is that ownership is settled before the shutter, not after.
